scope: Read-only source review by an agent separate from the collision/combat authors; no browser automation

resolved.issue: An OBB wider than its legacy index radius could be removed from segment candidates, changing a blocked result to clear.
resolved.resolution: If any OBB's circumradius plus the existing 0.002 collision epsilon exceeds its padded index radius, the navigator retains the original rectangle collector.
resolved.coverage: 220 underbound OBB cases and an epsilon boundary test; all four current map layouts retain the optimized path.

findings: Occlusion beforeRender keeps the original previous-frame comparison and reveal/flag ordering; Float64Array buffer reuse does not change GPU query code.
Combat reuse requires a same-generation proof, matching actor/map/navigation/terrain/radius and exact position before and after separation. Subclass movement invalidates the proof.
No additional high-risk difference or new unbounded retention was found in the current authored-map synchronous combat paths.
Player pose reuse was removed after paired CPU comparisons failed to show a consistent benefit.
limitations: Same-object in-place obstacle or terrain edits are not detected by reference checks. Current gameplay has no such edit during combat update; future dynamic terrain or layout code must invalidate the index/proof or use the original path.
This review does not measure hardware rendering, device FPS, GPU time or temperature.
